newsitem.title: USA: Bullet hole found in tail of TWA jet in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Bullet hole found in tail of TWA jet in Florida.

text.p: A Trans World Airlines Inc jet that had just flown from St. Louis was found to have a bullet hole in its tail after landing at Fort Lauderdale International Airport Thursday afternoon, police said.
No one was injured or in any danger in connection with the incident, an airline spokesman said.
The pilot of the Boeing 727 found the hole while making a routine inspection of the aircraft before its next flight, said a spokesman for the Broward County Sheriff's Office.
"The pilot discovered a hole in the tail section presumed to be a bullet hole," he said. "We checked the (airport) perimeter. We don't suspect anything suspicious or unusual."
The Federal Aviation Administration and TWA were investigating further. Local authorities speculated that the aircraft might have been hit while on its approach to the airport.
TWA spokesman Mark Abels said Flight 680 carried 120 passengers in addition to its crew to Fort Lauderdale.
He could not confirm that the hole was caused by a bullet. He stressed that there had been no indication of any anomolies during the trip from St. Louis.
